Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Samantha Cole (Redwood AE), Luis Martinez (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Rao (Vertex CISO), Mark Chen (VP Eng), Aisha Thompson (SecOps), Nina Patel (Legal), Jamal Ortiz (Platform)

Auto-generated sections (optional):
Topics: SOC2, ISO, PII/PHI handling, prompt retention, KMS, VPC, RBAC/SSO, audit logs

Transcript:
[00:00] Samantha Cole: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros \u0004 I'm Sam, AE at Redwood, with Luis our SE.
[00:06] Dr. Priya Rao: Hi, this is Priya, CISO at Vertex Health. We're looking to validate data handling before a pilot.
[00:10] Luis Martinez: Great, thanks. We'll jump into the controls you care about \u0004 retention, encryption, training guarantees, and deployment modes.
[00:18] Mark Chen: Timeline \u0004 we'd like to run a pilot in April and need assurances for PHI handling and legal review.
[00:22] Samantha Cole: Totally. We'll cover SOC 2 evidence and how Redwood prevents customer data from being used to train models.
[00:27] Jamal Ortiz: Quick note \u0004 we have an internal policy that explicit PII/PHI must not be retained beyond 30 days, and we need audit trails.
[00:34] Luis Martinez: Understood. On retention, Redwood offers configurable retention windows for request/response logs in the hosted service, and in Dedicated/Private you control retention entirely. By default hosted logs are retained 90 days for analytics, but we can redline that in a contract.
[00:50] Aisha Thompson: Are transcripts or prompts ever fed back into model training in your hosted product?
[00:55] Samantha Cole: Short answer: no. We have a customer data use policy \u0004 we do not use customer prompts or outputs to train underlying models. For clarity, we can provide the exact policy language and the SOC 2 description.
[01:06] Dr. Priya Rao: We need that in writing. Also want to confirm on stored embeddings and caches \u0004 are embeddings considered customer data and deleted on request?
[01:15] Luis Martinez: Yes \u0004 embeddings and KV/cache artifacts are treated as customer data. In Hosted, you can configure automatic deletion or disable persistence. In Dedicated and Private, you control lifecycle and can run with ephemeral caches only.
[01:28] Mark Chen: Encryption \u0004 at rest and in transit \u0004 what KMS options do you support? We use AWS KMS and an HSM for key material in other systems.
[01:36] Luis Martinez: We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and GCP KMS for private deployments. For Hosted, we provide envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys by default, and customer-managed KMS as an option for enterprise tenants. HSM integration for on-prem is possible in Private deployments.
[01:51] Nina Patel: For the contract we need a KMS key rotation policy and proof of encryption in transit (TLS version, ciphers).
[01:57] Samantha Cole: We'll share the crypto whitepaper and TLS configuration. We use TLS1.2+ and can provide cipher suites and cert rotation details.
[02:04] Aisha Thompson: Audit logs \u0004 we need immutable logs of who accessed prompts and model outputs and ability to export logs to our SIEM.
[02:12] Luis Martinez: Redwood's Console emits audit events for token/project/model access, login events, and admin actions. For Dedicated/Private you can route logs to your SIEM via syslog/Cloudwatch. Hosted supports log export to customer-owned buckets via S3 export and pub/sub options.
[02:30] Dr. Priya Rao: Are audit logs tamper-evident? We need chain-of-custody for compliance.
[02:34] Luis Martinez: We capture append-only events and sign them server-side. For high-assurance customers we can push events to a write-once storage or customer-controlled bucket to maintain immutability. I'll add that to the POC scope.
[02:47] Jamal Ortiz: On SSO and RBAC \u0004 we use SAML and SCIM. We need role mappings and least-privilege for operators and developers.
[02:54] Samantha Cole: Redwood supports SAML SSO, OIDC, and SCIM provisioning. RBAC is fine-grained \u0004 project, model, and route-level permissions. You can map SAML groups to roles and enforce MFA via SSO.
[03:10] Mark Chen: Data residency \u0004 Vertex needs data to remain in us-east-1. Can hosted tenants be locked to a region?
[03:15] Luis Martinez: Yes, we offer region pinning for enterprise tenants in hosted. For stricter controls, Dedicated or Private deployments in your VPC in us-east-1 guarantee residency.
[03:26] Dr. Priya Rao: I want confirmation: if we run in Hosted, will backups or replicas ever leave the region?
[03:31] Luis Martinez: Not for enterprise region-pinned deployments \u0004 backups are kept in-region. We'll provide the architecture diagram in the follow-up.
[03:39] Aisha Thompson: Let's talk about redaction and PII detection \u0004 can Redwood automatically redact PHI or is that customer responsibility?
[03:46] Connor Liu: We have built-in redaction tooling and can run pre-processing hooks to strip PII. We also recommend customer-side preprocessing for sensitive fields; for the POC we can enable automatic PII detectors and return both redacted output and the raw for audit (configurable).
[04:05] Dr. Priya Rao: Good, but we can't have raw PHI stored. If raw is needed for troubleshooting, it must be ephemeral and logged.
[04:12] Luis Martinez: Agreed \u0004 ephemeral-only, logged access, and deletion on demand.
[04:17] Nina Patel: Regarding 'not training on customer data' \u0004 do you have attestations/controls and how is that enforced across model providers?
[04:25] Samantha Cole: We maintain a contractual guarantee and technical controls. For Redwood-hosted models, the pipeline ensures model training datasets are isolated and our internal policy prohibits using customer prompts. For third-party models, we vet their terms and offer Private/Dedicated if vendor training is a concern. We'll send the legal attestation language.
[04:46] Mark Chen: What about downstream caching and internal logs that might be picked up by other monitoring systems \u0004 how do you prevent leakage through telemetry?
[04:53] Luis Martinez: Telemetry is aggregated and scrubbed; we don't include prompt/response payloads in aggregated metrics. Full payloads are only in the request logs with access controls and retention.
[05:02] Dr. Priya Rao: Are there penetration test reports or third-party assessments we can review?
[05:07] Samantha Cole: Yes, we have pen test summaries and a list of recent engagements; we'll attach those.
[05:12] Aisha Thompson: For the POC, we'd like a short checklist: 1) Confirm region and KMS config, 2) PII redaction rules, 3) audit log export to our SIEM, 4) performance benchmark with sample PHI-safe dataset.
[05:22] Luis Martinez: We'll draft that checklist. We'll also include a minimal perf test harness to measure latency and throughput with/without encryption and caching.
[05:30] Jamal Ortiz: If we need on-prem due to regulatory reasons, what is the timeline for a Private deployment?
[05:34] Samantha Cole: Private installations typically take 6-12 weeks depending on networking and HSM integration. We'll scope it in the POC planning.
[05:41] Nina Patel: Legal \u0004 we need a DPA mapping, breach notification timelines, and standard indemnity language.
[05:47] Samantha Cole: We'll surface the DPA template and our standard 72-hour breach notification clause.
[05:52] Mark Chen: Anything else from Redwood?
[05:54] Luis Martinez: One more technical note \u0004 KV cache and persistent embeddings can be disabled, and for strict PII constraints we recommend Dedicated with ephemeral caches.
[06:03] Dr. Priya Rao: OK. To recap, we'll get SOC2/ISO docs, KMS and TLS details, pen test reports, and a POC plan with perf benchmarks and PII rules. Vertex will provide redaction rules and legal redlines.
[06:16] Samantha Cole: Correct. We'll send artifacts by Friday and propose POC dates for mid-April.
[06:22] Mark Chen: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[06:25] Samantha Cole: Thanks \u0004 we'll follow up with links and the action items.

End of transcript.
